title: Parameter for a line that just meets a parabola
source: Theory P1-1.9 Quick check 1 (y=2x+k meets y=x^2 at one point when k=-1); book Worked example 1.20 style p.28, new numbers
stem: Find the value of \(k\) for which the line \(y={m|int}x+k\) meets the curve \(y=x^2\) at exactly one point.

steps.name: A
steps.note: disc = m^2 + 4k = 0 gives k=-m^2/4. m is even so k is an integer. Original m=2, k=-1.

title: How many meeting points
source: Theory P1-1.9 Quick check 2 (y=x+2 meets y=x^2 twice); book substitution method p.27, new numbers
stem: How many times do the line \(y=x+{c|int}\) and the curve \(y=x^2\) meet?

steps.name: A
steps.text_tex: \(x^2-x-{c|int}=0\) has discriminant \(1+4\times {c|int}>0\), so they meet twice.
steps.note: For every c>=1 the discriminant 1+4c is positive, so the count is always 2.

title: x-coordinate of the unique meeting point
source: Theory P1-1.9 Quick check 3 (y=2x-1 meets y=x^2 at x=1); book Worked example 1.20 style p.28, new numbers
stem: The line \(y={m|int}x+({K|int})\) meets \(y=x^2\) at exactly one point. What is the \(x\)-coordinate of that point?

steps.name: A
steps.note: The unique root is x=m/2. Original m=2, K=-1, H=1. K in the stem is the already-computed intercept, written as an integer (negative).

contexts.note: Includes the original m=2, K=-1, H=1

title: A line and a parabola: no common points, or a unique meeting point

source.note: Stem taken from the QP PDF (UCLES 2010), Question 6 both parts. Official answers and mark allocation from the MS PDF. The item is paper/self-mark.

stem:
This question is 9709/12/O/N/10 Question 6, taken from the official QP.

A curve has equation \(y=kx^2+1\) and a line has equation \(y=kx\), where \(k\) is a non-zero constant.

(i) Find the set of values of \(k\) for which the curve and the line have no common points.  [3]

(ii) State the value of \(k\) for which the line is a tangent to the curve and, for this case, find the coordinates of the point where the line touches the curve.  [4]

steps.name: M0
steps.note: First mark of (i): form the quadratic in x. The printed scheme groups (i) as [3].

steps.name: M1
steps.text_tex: The discriminant is \(k^2-4k\). For no common points, \(k^2-4k<0\).
steps.note: MS (i): M1 for applying b^2-4ac with an inequality.

steps.name: A1
steps.note: MS (i): 0<k<4 A1 co. Independent check: k(k-4)<0 iff 0<k<4. Together these three marks are the official [3] for part (i).

steps.name: B1
steps.text_tex: The line meets the curve at exactly one point when the discriminant is zero and \(k\neq 0\), so \(k=4\).
steps.note: MS (ii): k=4 only, B1 follow-through from their k^2-4k=0, not k=0. The official stem uses the word tangent; that wording is kept verbatim in the stem only.

steps.name: M2
steps.note: MS (ii): M1 for (2x-1)^2=0, follow-through from their k.

steps.name: A
steps.note: MS (ii): A1 for y=2, or for the point (1/2, 2). Part (ii) is B1 M1 A1 A1, totalling 4. The whole item is 7 marks. Independent check: at k=4, x=1/2 and y=kx=2, and also y=kx^2+1=2.
